source_audit.scope: NYC Department of Buildings and NYC Open Data records for 2008-2026 architecture/building-status candidate events.

duplicate_screening.method: Searched canonical manual milestones and prior NYC subagent files by project name, address, and likely event slug before accepting candidates.
duplicate_screening.note: Accepted records are DOB-observed administrative changes. They should be merged carefully with public-opening events if later corroborated by owner, architect, or agency pages.

sources.publisher: NYC Department of Buildings via NYC Open Data
sources.license: NYC Open Data / NYC.gov terms; factual metadata cited only
sources.limitations: DOB NOW CO records begin with the March 2021 module. CO issuance confirms legal occupancy status for the recorded application, but does not by itself prove public opening, full tenant move-in, design authorship, or final completion of all building work.

sources.publisher: NYC Department of Buildings via NYC Open Data
sources.license: NYC Open Data / NYC.gov terms; factual metadata cited only
sources.limitations: Legacy CO dataset covers certificates issued from July 2012 to March 2021. It may include repeated temporary COs and address-normalization differences.

sources.publisher: NYC Department of Buildings via NYC Open Data
sources.license: NYC Open Data / NYC.gov terms; factual metadata cited only
sources.limitations: Permit records document approved or issued work permits, not completion. Avoid treating construction fences, sheds, or minor fit-outs as building-status changes unless tied to a known major project.

selection_notes: Prioritized new-building or Alteration Type 1 CO records over repeated minor permit records.
Used temporary COs as observed occupancy/legal-use milestones, not as final completion claims.
Rejected DOB records where the same project milestone already appears in the manual architecture milestone file.
